 KrisFlyer News Scoot ScootPlus cabin joining the KrisFlyer award chart in 2027
 by Andrew 20 November 2026, 12:30 20 November 2026, 12:35 
 Leave a Comment on ScootPlus cabin joining the KrisFlyer award chart in 2027 
 ScootPlus is joining the KrisFlyer award chart from early 2027, opening up fixed-price redemptions in the carrier’s Boeing 787 premium cabin. 
Here’s what you get, where it flies and why it could cost less than SIA Economy. 
 Alongside the 2027 shake-up of KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards and PPS Rewards, Singapore Airlines slipped in another announcement this week that may prove useful for many of our readers – from early 2027, Scoot will extend its fixed-price KrisFlyer award chart to include ScootPlus, its premium cabin on the Boeing 787 fleet.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 Since Scoot first launched its award chart in August 2025, chart-based redemptions on the low-cost carrier’s flights have been in Economy Class only.
 Plenty of our readers don’t want to spend their hard-earned KrisFlyer miles on the “basic” Scoot Economy experience – with bags, meals and Wi-Fi all costing extra.
 A leather recliner in a 2-3-2 layout with 38 inches of pitch, a 30kg checked bag, a meal and a free drink might change that, especially on longer flights to Japan, Korea, Australia and Europe, and sometimes even on a shorter hop to Bali or Bangkok, where it arguably brings the service experience closer to Singapore Airlines Economy Class, but with a much more spacious seat.
 Rates haven’t been published yet, so here’s what ScootPlus offers, which routes actually have it, and what we think the awards might end up costing, once this option launches.
 What’s been announced
 SIA’s programme updates page confirms that from early 2027, Scoot will enhance its award chart to “enable members to redeem ScootPlus award flights as well” .
 As with Scoot Economy awards, these will be fixed-rate redemptions, bookable on flyscoot.com or via the Scoot app, when logged in as a KrisFlyer member.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 There’s no firm date (just “early 2027”), and no rates yet. For now, Scoot’s KrisFlyer page still says ScootPlus award redemptions and upgrades to ScootPlus are not available, and the current award T&Cs confirm that award flights can’t be upgraded to ScootPlus.
 What is ScootPlus?
 ScootPlus is Scoot’s premium cabin. It is only installed on the carrier’s wide-body Boeing 787-8 and Boeing 787-9 aircraft, and isn’t available on its single-aisle A320, A321 or E190 fleets.
 In fact, on a typical day only 1 in 4 Scoot flights from Singapore features ScootPlus, and overall less than 3% of its departing seats across the network are ScootPlus – 97% are Economy.
 (Image: Scoot) 
 Instead of the 3-3-3 layout in Scoot Economy on the 787, ScootPlus has a 2-3-2 layout, featuring TIMCO leather recliner seats, with adjustable headrests and footrests.
 ScootPlus seats on Scoot’s Boeing 787 have a generous 8-inch recline.

 KrisFlyer award space should be more generous on the 787-9 flights, which have 35 ScootPlus seats compared to just 18 or 21 on the smaller 787-8s.

 Couple seats
 The pairs of seats by the window (A/C and H/K) are a nice selling point for couples travelling together. In Scoot Economy on the 787, it’s a 3-3-3 configuration, useless for couples apart from a row or two at the very back where it narrows to 2-3-2.
 A ScootPlus window pair.
(Photo: MainlyMiles) 
 Singapore Airlines Economy Class is no better these days when it comes to couple seats. Since the A330s (in 2-4-2 configuration) left the fleet, 3-3-3 or 3-4-3 is now the norm in this cabin on the mainline carrier.
 Power
 ScootPlus has 110V universal AC power sockets, with one per seat, so there’s no fighting over them with your neighbour.
 ScootPlus power socket.
(Photo: MainlyMiles)

 Add-ons can’t be paid with miles on a Scoot Economy award, only with cash, but they are bundled into the ScootPlus base fare, and therefore the future miles award price too.
 Since these features will all be included, the value of a ScootPlus award may often be higher than the gap in the seat comfort alone suggests, particularly if you’d otherwise be paying for a checked bag and a meal when flying on a Scoot Economy award.
 Last time I flew ScootPlus the free Wi-Fi allowance was only 30MB. Thankfully that’s improved, but you’ll still churn through 200MB pretty quickly! 
 Which routes have ScootPlus?
 ScootPlus is available on any route that features the airline’s Boeing 787 on at least one regular flight. Some routes have a mix of 787 and single-aisle flights, so check the aircraft type when you search.
 You can only book ScootPlus on the 787 flights in these cases (e.g. KL, Bali and Bangkok have both 787 and single-aisle flights).

 One-way award rates from Singapore in Economy Class 
 Scoot’s Boeing 787 routes with ScootPlus, November 2026 
 Scoot also flies fifth freedom routes to and from Taipei with the 787, to Tokyo Narita, Seoul Incheon and Sapporo. These are in the award chart’s Zone 17, currently priced at 9,500 miles Saver and 15,000 miles Advantage in Economy. ScootPlus awards should be possible on those flights too, from early next year.
 Scoot’s 787s also serve Jeddah, but that route is currently suspended and is excluded from the award chart anyway.
 What might ScootPlus awards cost?
 Scoot hasn’t revealed any rates for ScootPlus redemptions yet.
 Currently its award chart has both Saver and Advantage rates for Economy Class, which could be replicated with two rates for ScootPlus also in the mix, or the airline might only offer Saver rates for ScootPlus, like Singapore Airlines does for its small Premium Economy cabins.
 How much more ScootPlus awards will cost compared to Economy is anyone’s guess, but we’ve had a go at one anyway!
 We looked at the lowest cash fares on 63 Scoot flights and 81 Singapore Airlines flights over a week, six months from now, on a five-city mix of regional and long-haul routes.
 Excluding taxes (which miles don’t cover anyway), ScootPlus typically cost around double the Economy fare on regional and North Asian routes like Bali, Bangkok and Tokyo, but nearly four times as much on long-haul flights to Sydney and Athens.
 ScootPlus can sometimes cost only slightly more than Economy on the same flight, probably when Economy is filling up fast but ScootPlus isn’t.
 ScootPlus for just S$70 more than Economy to Bangkok. Simply adding a 20kg checked bag to the Economy fare costs S$40 on this route, or S$54 for the same 30kg allowance as ScootPlus! 
 On SIA, Premium Economy sets you back anywhere from about 80% to 200% more than Economy in cash on comparable routes. Yet the Premium Economy Saver award only costs 55% to 89% more miles than Economy – roughly half the cash difference .
 That’s still enough to put SIA Premium Economy closer to Business Class than Economy in miles on many routes, which is why we seldom recommend Premium Economy redemptions.

ScootPlus figures are our own estimates, not published rates.
SIA doesn’t offer Premium Economy awards to Bangkok or Bali. 
 On regional and North Asian routes, ScootPlus awards could well come in cheaper than SIA Economy Saver , with a wider 38 inch pitch recliner, plus a checked bag and a meal included.
 Tokyo or Seoul for around 18,000 – 20,000 miles would compare quite favourably with 25,500 miles in SIA Economy.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 For a ScootPlus Saver award to Tokyo or Seoul to cost more than SIA Economy Saver, Scoot would need to more than double its Economy rate. That’s a bigger premium than SIA itself charges for Premium Economy awards over Economy on any route (55% to 89%).
 On Australia and Europe, where ScootPlus commands a much bigger premium in cash, rates could land around the same as SIA Economy Saver to Sydney and Melbourne, and a bit higher to Athens and Vienna. They should still be well short of SIA Premium Economy Saver though, for what is effectively a Premium Economy seat, albeit without the service bells and whistles.
 The main trade-off is really flexibility , since Scoot awards are non-refundable except in limited circumstances, while SIA awards can be refunded for a fee.
 We’ll stress that the estimated rates are guesswork on our part . Scoot doesn’t have to follow SIA’s lead, and could price ScootPlus higher or lower than our estimate, but hopefully it gives a reasonable idea of what to expect.
 Remember too that these are small cabins, with only 18 to 35 seats per flight, so Scoot will naturally want to sell as many of them as it can for cash, or as paid upgrades. That may well limit award space.
 For context, we looked at every Scoot departure from Singapore on Thursday 19th November 2026. Of 92 flights that day, only 23 were operated by a Boeing 787 with a ScootPlus cabin, offering 605 ScootPlus seats between them – just 2.9% of the airline’s 21,025 departing seats across the day , or fewer than 1 in 34.
 You can already use miles for ScootPlus (but don’t)
 It’s already possible to use KrisFlyer miles towards a ScootPlus flight, at a fixed 1 cent per mile off the cash price, which is the only way Scoot Economy redemptions used to work before the award chart was launched.
 You can pay this S$496 ScootPlus fare with 49,600 KrisFlyer miles 
 At 1 cent per mile this is poor value, and not something we’d ever recommend, though you can cover all the taxes and fees with miles in this case rather than paying for them on top if you choose, or use the slider to offset only a portion of the fare, for example when cashing out orphan or expiring miles.
 ScootPlus to join Spontaneous Escapes?
 When Scoot launched its award chart, we predicted that fixed rates would open the door to the budget airline’s flights joining KrisFlyer’s Spontaneous Escapes promotion. Scoot Economy awards then duly became part of the monthly deal in April 2026 .
 There’s no reason ScootPlus awards can’t follow too, once they have fixed rates, likely discounted by 15%, as Scoot Economy awards currently are during this monthly promotion. Let’s hope it doesn’t take them eight months to do so this time round.
 That would add another discounted award option to the monthly deal, with a better seat, a checked bag and a meal all covered by the miles. Since even SIA Spontaneous Escapes awards are non-refundable, it could provide a nice alternative to an Economy Promo award on ‘overlap’ routes like Bangkok and Bali.
 What about upgrade awards?
 Currently, Scoot does not offer upgrade awards for cash tickets, nor can award flights be upgraded to ScootPlus using miles.
 That’s fair enough – there is no ScootPlus award inventory to tap at the moment, so this is probably impractical – for now.
 ADVERTISEMENT 
 A ScootPlus upgrade award chart for Economy ticket holders would be a nice addition, subject to Saver (or Advantage, if they have it) award space in the ScootPlus cabin on the same flight.
 However, SIA’s announcement only mentions ScootPlus award flights, and Scoot likes to keep things simple , so we wouldn’t bet on a separate upgrade award chart, at least not initially.
 Our award prices page
 Our KrisFlyer award prices by route page already shows Scoot award rates alongside Singapore Airlines rates for every destination on both carriers’ networks.
 Here’s the tool showing only Scoot routes, with the current Saver and Advantage Economy rates.

 We’ll add the ScootPlus rates as soon as the airline publishes them, so you can compare all the options in one place, city-by-city.
 Summary
 ScootPlus awards could be a useful new option for KrisFlyer members, particularly those who’ve steered clear of Scoot awards because of the no-frills experience.
 A 38 inch pitch recliner in a 2-3-2 layout, with a checked bag, a meal and Wi-Fi included, is a very different proposition from Scoot Economy, especially on six to eight hour flights to North Asia and Australia.
 The value will depend on the rates Scoot sets and how many seats it releases. If Scoot follows SIA’s Economy / Premium Economy differentials, ScootPlus awards could cost fewer miles than SIA Economy Saver on many regional and North Asian routes, around the same on Australia, and a bit more on Europe, though still well short of SIA Premium Economy.
 That’s not confirmed yet of course, but we’ll update you with the actual rates as soon as they’re published.
